headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line, yet MACD is turning up and ETF desks keep buying
paragraphs: Start with the trend map, because it's unanimous: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day moving averages, and none show a golden cross. BTC is 48.7% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is down 61.0% from $4,817.76, and the small-caps in this basket are worse: SOL -69.2%, XRP -68.9%, DOGE -75.9%, ADA -79.8%. When seven-for-seven sit under the long-term trend line, that's not noise from one weak asset, that's the whole complex still working through a drawdown regardless of what any single day's candle looks like.

Momentum tells a different, more interesting story. RSI-14 readings are mostly mid-range and unremarkable (BTC 49.0, ETH 50.4, SOL 55.0, BNB 61.8), nobody's overbought or oversold. But MACD has crossed above signal for BTC, SOL, BNB, DOGE and ADA, meaning short-term momentum is firming even while long-term trend remains negative. That's a genuine divergence worth naming: price structure says bear market, momentum says a recovery attempt is underway. ETH and XRP haven't gotten that MACD flip yet, so the split isn't universal. ADA is the standout here, up 15.33% over 7 days and 35.2% over 30, RSI at 62.7, clearly running hotter than its peers despite sitting furthest from its 12-month high.

Positioning adds texture. Funding is positive across the board (annualized around 11% for BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE on OKX), meaning longs are paying shorts to hold their bets, a modest but consistent tilt toward bullish leverage. The long/short account ratio confirms the crowd is stacked long, and it gets more extreme down the cap ladder: BTC 1.35, ETH 1.78, SOL 2.0, XRP 3.69, DOGE 5.25. That crowding showed up in liquidations: over the past 22-23 hours, BTC longs lost $12.5M versus $1.9M for shorts, and ETH longs lost $13.7M versus $4.2M for shorts. Open interest remains sizable ($2.04B on BTC, $1.41B on ETH), so there's real money in the boat, and today's red candles caught the long side leaning the wrong way.

On the flow side, the traditional-finance bid is still present: BTC spot ETFs took in $101.7M on 07 Aug, part of a $865.3M net over the last five sessions with all five days in the same direction. ETH ETFs added $49.6M that day, $243.7M over five sessions, four of five days net positive. Whale wallets moved $60.2M net off exchanges in BTC over 24 hours, consistent with accumulation, though the weekly series behind it ($291.8M, $701.7M, $1.07B, then -$89.7M) shows the most recent day actually flipped toward exchanges after three strong outflow days, so call that trend cooling rather than broken. Stablecoin float sits at $306.3B, down 1.12% over 30 days, a slight drain in the dry powder sitting on the sidelines.

Against all that, the Fear & Greed Index reads 30, labeled Fear, sitting near the top of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. So the crowd feels cautious even as ETF desks keep printing net buys and whale wallets have spent most of the past few days pulling coin off exchanges. That gap between sentiment and money flow is the day's real tension: fear on the surface, accumulation underneath, at least until that last day's whale reversal is confirmed or denied by tomorrow's print.

What to watch from here: whether MACD's bullish cross on BTC, SOL, BNB, DOGE and ADA survives another session or fades back under signal, whether the whale flow returns to net outflow after that single negative day, and whether funding stays positive without spiking, since crowded long positioning plus a funding spike is usually the combination that produces the kind of liquidation cascade already visible in today's numbers.
